Update: after reviewing the source material for the algorithm, I believe that the docstring and code comment are correct, and the code itself should be fixed by replacing the '>' with a '<', like so:

``` python
n_samples, n_features = M.shape

if transpose == 'auto' and n_samples < n_features:
   transpose = True
```

I agree, but there is still a bug.
The data is transposed in any case!

``` python
if transpose="auto" and some_condition:
    transpose = True
# if transpose was "auto", it is now either True or "auto".
if transpose:
   # always true if "auto" was given
```

Gna!

Not sure how to do a regression test for this. Maybe (this is how I found it), create a skinny matrix, run it with auto, transpose, run it with auto, and see that they take approximately the same time. That depends on the load of the system, though, so it is probably a bad idea.

issue.title: [MRG] Fix randomized_svd transpose heuristic.
issue.body:
Fixes #4455.
This fixes two things: the heuristic (`<` vs `>`) and a logic error (the `"auto"` also evaluates to `True`)
As this is a performance optimization, I don't know how to regression-test it.
I did something like this:

``` python
from sklearn.utils.extmath import randomized_svd
import numpy as np
X = np.dot(np.random.normal(size=(10000, 25)), np.random.normal(size=(25, 200)))
%timeit randomized_svd(X, n_components=10, transpose='auto')
```

body: See #4478 for a fix for both.

> Not sure how to do a regression test for this. Maybe (this is how I found it), create a skinny matrix, run it with auto, transpose, run it with auto, and see that they take approximately the same time.

Can you not just check for strict equality of `randomized_svd(skinny_matrix, transpose='auto')` and randomized_svd(skinny_matrix.T, transpose=False)`? If they match exactly that must mean that the matrix was indeed transposed with transpose='auto'.
@lesteve yeah, that is right. I think the main reason we haven't merged #4478 is that there were numeric changes in the results and no-one checked if they were bad.

issue.title: possible bug in scikit-learn\sklearn\utils\extmath.py the transpose='auto' option in randomised_svd
issue.body:
#### Description
In scikit-learn\sklearn\utils\extmath.py the transpose='auto' option in randomised_svd apparently makes the eigenvalue problem larger, rather than smaller.  I believe the goal is to make matrix_size = min (n_samples, n_features), not max. It needs double-checking. The result should be the same either way, just takes longer to run for no good reason. 

The current code is

    if transpose == 'auto':
        transpose = n_samples < n_features

while I suspect that it should be the opposite

    if transpose == 'auto':
        transpose = n_samples > n_features

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce
Any example running randomised_svd on non-square data matrix. 

#### Expected Results
The transpose='auto' option in randomised_svd should make the matrix size smaller for the eigenvalue problem solved by the power method in randomised_svd, so it runs faster. 

#### Actual Results
The transpose='auto' option in randomised_svd should make the matrix size larger, rather than smaller.

#### Versions
sklearn: 0.21.dev0
